blocks.text: The PNS makes sensory pathways, the sensory neurons of cranial and spinal nerves that connect receptors to the CNS, and motor pathways, the motor neurons that connect the CNS to the effectors. The motor pathways form two systems.

items: Somatic nervous system: the motor neurons of spinal and cranial nerves that control skeletal muscles. It is voluntary, so skeletal muscles move at will, though in reflex actions it works without conscious control.

Autonomic nervous system: the motor neurons that control smooth muscles and glands. It is involuntary and controls internal conditions such as breathing, heartbeat and digestion. It has two divisions.

Sympathetic nervous system: prepares the body under physical or emotional stress. Its motor neurons start in the thoracic and lumbar regions of the spinal cord and reach the visceral organs; when it is active the body is ready for fight or flight: the heart beats faster and stronger, blood glucose rises, blood is diverted to the muscles and heart, and the bronchioles widen.

Parasympathetic nervous system: opposes the sympathetic response once the threat or stress has passed. Its motor neurons start in the brain and the sacral region of the spinal cord, many of them in the vagus (tenth cranial) nerve; it brings the organs back to normal: the heart slows, blood flow to the heart and skeletal muscles falls, and digestive organs become more active.
